issues.legal_issue: The statutory revisional power over rent-control orders extends beyond review for jurisdictional error.
material_facts: A landlord sought revision of an appellate order under the rent-control statute.
The High Court treated its revisional power as equivalent to the restricted power under the ordinary civil procedure provision and found no jurisdictional question.
The Supreme Court considered the wording of the statutory revisional provision.
issues.conclusion: The revisional power is wider than the ordinary civil procedure revision power and is not confined to questions of jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: The provision governing revision in section 15(5) authorizes examination of the legality or propriety of orders or proceedings and permits such further order as the High Court deems fit; its scope is wider than section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

predicates.statutory_rent_control_revision: A party seeks revision under a statutory rent-control scheme.
predicates.challenged_rent_control_order: The revision challenges an order or proceeding made under that rent-control scheme.
predicates.revision_review_is_not_limited_to_jurisd: The reviewing court may examine more than whether the lower authority acted within its jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When a rent-control order is challenged through statutory revision, the review is not limited to jurisdictional questions.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord may obtain possession for building work only when the work is sufficiently extensive and fundamental that it cannot be carried out while the tenant remains in possession.
material_facts: The landlord sought possession to replace or repair a cracked pillar pursuant to a local authority's requirement.
The local authority later required only that a doorway in the pillar be filled with masonry to make the pillar solid.
The tenant carried out the repair, and an inspecting engineer found it satisfactory.
The repair could be carried out without requiring the tenant to vacate.
issues.conclusion: The minor repair did not justify requiring the tenant to surrender possession; the statutory ground applies only to work that cannot be carried out with the tenant in possession.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(3)(a)(iii), read in light of the scheme and purpose of the legislation, requires that the landlord actually need vacant possession for the building work. The work must be fundamental and extensive enough that it cannot be done while the tenant remains; minor repairs do not meet that requirement.

rule.if: tenant_eviction_for_building_work and public_authority_required_work and work_is_fundamental_and_extensive and work_cannot_be_done_with_tenant_in_possession

predicates.tenant_eviction_for_building_work: A landlord seeks to evict a tenant so that building work can be carried out.
predicates.public_authority_required_work: A public authority required the building work.
predicates.work_is_fundamental_and_extensive: The required work is fundamental and extensive rather than a minor repair.
predicates.work_cannot_be_done_with_tenant_in_posse: The work cannot be carried out while the tenant remains in possession.
predicates.landlord_may_obtain_possession_for_build: The landlord may obtain possession so the qualifying building work can be carried out.

issues.definition: A landlord may obtain possession for building work only when a public authority required fundamental and extensive work that cannot be done while the tenant remains in possession.

issues.legal_issue: In deciding whether possession is required for building work, the court may consider events occurring after the eviction application but before the date possession is to take effect.
material_facts: The local authority modified its repair requirement after the landlord filed the eviction application.
Before the date set for the tenant to vacate, the tenant completed the repair and an inspecting engineer found it satisfactory.
The appellate authority considered those later events when deciding whether the landlord required possession.
issues.conclusion: The appellate authority was entitled to consider events occurring up to the time when the order for possession was to take effect.
issues.legal_principle: Having regard to the scheme and purpose of the legislation, and to the requirement that the landlord's claim be bona fide when possession is ordered to take effect, the court may consider facts existing at that time, including events after the application was filed.

predicates.tenant_eviction_for_building_work: A landlord seeks to evict a tenant so that building work can be carried out.
predicates.relevant_event_occurred_before_possessio: An event relevant to the need for possession occurred after the application but before the date possession was to take effect.
predicates.later_pre_possession_events_may_be_consi: The court may consider relevant events occurring before the date possession was to take effect.

issues.definition: In a building-work eviction proceeding, the court may consider relevant events occurring before the date possession is to take effect.
